draft.title: Cloning
card: A clone is a genetically identical copy of a gene, a cell or a whole organism. Cloning can be done on any of these three levels.
Many plants clone themselves, and growers copy this with cuttings. A piece of stem is cut off and grown into a new plant with the same genes as the parent.

In somatic cell nuclear transfer, the nucleus of an egg cell is removed. A nucleus from a body cell of the animal to be copied is put in its place. The egg is then triggered to divide and grow into an embryo.
Dolly the sheep, born in 1996, was the first mammal cloned from an adult body cell. Her nuclear DNA came from the donor sheep, so she was genetically identical to that sheep in her nuclear genes.
draft.remember: A clone carries the same genes as its source, whether it is a gene, a cell or a whole organism.

a.q: Why is a plant grown from a cutting genetically identical to its parent plant?
opts: It grows from the parent's own cells, with no gene mixing
It grows from a seed made by two parent plants
It is given the parent's genes by an added chemical
It is exposed to the same soil and sunlight as the parent
a.why: A cutting grows from the parent's body cells, so it has the same genes and no genes are mixed from another plant. Growing in the same conditions does not make plants genetically identical, because genes come only from the cells that grow into the new plant.
a.clue: Think about whose cells grow into the new plant.

b.q: A nucleus from a cell in the udder of sheep X is placed in an egg cell from sheep Y, after Y's nucleus is removed. The egg grows into a lamb. Whose nuclear genes does the lamb carry?
opts: An equal mix from sheep X and sheep Y
Sheep X and its father, as in normal breeding
b.why: The nucleus holds the cell's nuclear DNA, and it came from sheep X, so the lamb is a clone of X. Sheep Y gave the egg cell but its nucleus was removed, so Y's nuclear genes are not passed on. No fertilisation took place, so there is no mixing of genes.
b.clue: Which nucleus was left in the egg cell?

a.best: It grows from the parent's own cells, with no gene mixing
